gddGap: The GDD lists Rust Grunts, 'The Iron Line', for crowd control and frontline combat, but the Tier 0 rust-grunt is the only canon stat block. This is the Iron Line's crowd-control variant: a grunt that holds a line and sweeps a wide arc, so waves can pin the lane without adding a new silhouette. The base Iron Line unit remains rust-grunt (canon). FINAL BALANCE (tuned against the combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms telegraph as the Tier 0 anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms): 36 HP is about 5 light hits, same damage as the grunt, 500 ms wind-up so the wide sweep reads one beat slower. Final.
name: Rust Iron Line Cordon
description: A Rust grunt of the Iron Line in cheap rust-coated slate plating, a plain steel helmet with a cyan visor and no personal marks, because the helmets hide who they are. Same boxy, symmetrical build as the grunt, with a gunmetal push-bar held across the chest.
behaviour: Moves in at grunt speed and stops at the front of the group to hold the lane, trying to pin Zed against his own crowd. Uses one wide sweep with the push-bar that shoves Zed back along the lane. Counts against the attacker cap like any other attacker, and never attacks from behind. When Zed gets too close or grabs too often it answers with the grunt Helmet Headbutt (short wind-up, brief stun) from the GDD Iron Line move list.
telegraph: 500 ms wind-up: both arms pull the bar to one side, the red telegraph icon pops above the head, the body tints red and the outline thickens. The sweep is wide, so the red ground arc shows its reach.
weakness: Low health and a short reach in depth. Step out of the lane (dodge) or block the shove, then punish in the recovery window. Heavy attacks from the side skip its guard-stance and juggle it clear of the line.

gddGap: The GDD defines Rust Bruisers, "The Breakers": massive shock troops on muscle stimulants (former criminals promised freedom for loyalty) for area denial, with three named moves: Gauntlet Smash, Rust Uppercut and Body Check. It gives no stats. The stat block and telegraph timings are proposed; the three moves are canon. Open question for the combat contract: ground bounce, block-break and super armour do not exist in the engine yet. Merged: replaces rust-enforcer. FINAL BALANCE (tuned against the combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms telegraph as the Tier 0 anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms): 90 HP is about 5 heavy hits, 16 damage is two grunt hits, 700 ms wind-up and 1100 ms recovery give a big punish window. Final.
name: Rust Breaker
description: A hulking Rust Bruiser in heavily reinforced slate and steel plating, with a massive squared-off silhouette, a small helmet and a cyan visor. Cold, symmetrical and boxy; massive shock trooper enhanced with illegal muscle stimulants, built to crush resistance groups. A gunmetal brace on each forearm.
behaviour: Walks slowly straight at Zed, ignoring the circling rules, and takes an attacker slot when one is free. Plants its feet and slams both braces into the floor, leaving a short patch of rattled ground in front of it that Zed should stay out of for a moment (area denial). Long recovery after every slam. Cannot be juggled while winding up, so the player must dodge, not just mash. GDD move list. 1) Gauntlet Smash: downward smash with a reinforced gauntlet, medium startup, causes ground bounce, breaks player block, signature thud on impact (this is the slam above). 2) Rust Uppercut: a rising punch that launches Zed and works as an anti-air option; used when Zed jumps too often. 3) Body Check: a shoulder slam with plated armour, a short forward dash that knocks Zed back, can interrupt combos, and has super armour during the dash.
telegraph: 700 ms wind-up: both braces raised overhead, telegraph icon scaled 1.4 times and a large red ground danger ellipse at 30 percent alpha showing the slam area, per the heavy-enemy cue.
weakness: Big, slow and predictable. Dodge out of the red ellipse, then land a full combo in the long recovery. Heavy attacks stagger it; blocking works but the shove-back is large. Do not try to trade hits during the Body Check dash (super armour): sidestep it. Stop jumping in on it, or the Uppercut answers. Block does not hold against the Smash (it breaks block), so dodge it.

gddGap: The GDD defines Rust Rangers, "The Watchers": agile units with taser rifles, batons and tracking visors that scan heat signatures, for long-range harassment, pursuit and reconnaissance, with two named moves: Taser Shot and Baton Strike. It gives no stats. Stats are proposed. Conflict to resolve: the GDD gives the Baton Strike a "very quick startup", but the readability rule keeps telegraphs at 300 ms or more, so this entry uses 350 ms. Merged: replaces rust-dart-marksman and rust-baton-scout. FINAL BALANCE (tuned against the combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms telegraph as the Tier 0 anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms): 28 HP (fragile, rewards closing in), 7 damage per bolt, 650 ms taser wind-up, 350 ms baton wind-up. Final.
name: Rust Watcher
description: A lean, agile Rust Ranger in a slate uniform with a gunmetal taser rifle, a baton at the belt and a wide tracking visor with a cyan scan line. Symmetrical and boxy, but lighter than the grunt.
behaviour: Stays at range, strafing along the far side of the arena and following Zed with its visor. Fires a single slow taser bolt along the lane when it holds an attacker slot, then relocates. If Zed closes in it backs off, and only swings the baton when cornered. A hunter built to harass rebels at range and chase them down. GDD move list. Taser Shot: a quick electric bolt, light damage, brief stun on hit, used constantly to harass and to encourage Zed to close distance. Baton Strike: a fast electrified-baton hit with very quick startup that interrupts combos, used when Zed gets too close. Lore: trained to track rebels through alleyways and rooftops; the visor scans heat signatures, so hiding barely works.
telegraph: 650 ms wind-up for the taser: rifle raised, a cyan scan line draws along the floor toward Zed, and the red telegraph icon pops above the head. The bolt is slow enough to sidestep. The baton swing uses a 350 ms wind-up with the standard cues.
weakness: Low health. Sidestep out of the lane to dodge, then close the gap; juggle routes that carry Zed across the arena reach it fast. Blocking the bolt is also possible but eats a chip of damage.

gddGap: The GDD defines Rust Specialists, "The Copper Fangs": elite soldiers with electrified gauntlets, grappling hooks and tactical shields, Varr's personal favourites, conditioned to remove fear and hesitation, for high-priority targets and boss-tier encounters. The GDD now lists three Basic Attacks (Fang Jab, Copper Cross, Shield Bash), which are canon; the shield-breaking, grappling-hook and two-phase mini-boss structure and every number here are proposed. Merged: replaces rust-shield-sergeant. Tier 3. FINAL BALANCE (tuned against the combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms telegraph as the Tier 0 anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms): 140 HP, 15 damage, 650 ms wind-up, 750 ms hook. Numbers final.
name: Rust Copper Fang
description: An elite Rust Specialist in a sharper slate uniform with copper-toned gauntlets, a tactical shield strapped to one arm and a grappling hook launcher on the other. Still cold, symmetrical and boxy, with a narrow cyan visor. Psychological conditioning has removed all fear and hesitation: an elite hunter sent to eliminate priority targets.
behaviour: Two-phase mini-boss. Phase one: advances behind the shield, blocking front light hits, then lunges with a gauntlet strike. Phase two (below half health): fires a grappling hook that yanks Zed a short way across the lane, followed by a gauntlet jab. Calls for an attacker slot before every move so it never stacks with a full cap. Hitstun scales down while it is shielded so juggles cannot loop it (boss immunity, see adversarial-qa#2). GDD Basic Attacks ("Sharp, Controlled, Professional"). 1) Fang Jab: a lightning-quick electrified gauntlet jab with very fast startup and brief stun on hit, used to interrupt player combos. 2) Copper Cross: a cross-punch with crackling electricity, medium damage, causes stagger, used after dodging a player attack (the Fang answers Zed's dodges with it). 3) Shield Bash: a forward shove with the tactical shield that pushes Zed back and breaks guard, used to create space for follow-up attacks.
telegraph: 650 ms wind-up for the gauntlet lunge: gauntlet drawn back and crackling, telegraph icon scaled 1.4 times with a red ground zone. The hook has a 750 ms wind-up: the launcher is raised and a thin cyan line shows the path, plus the red icon. Fang Jab: 320 ms wind-up, the shortest the readability rule allows, with the red icon and a spark on the gauntlet. Copper Cross: 500 ms, crackling arm drawn back. Shield Bash: 550 ms, shield pulled in and a red ground strip in front.
weakness: Heavy attacks break the shield. Parry the lunge or dodge the hook line to open it, then juggle in the recovery window. Rewards the skill-depth pillar: block, dodge and parry all have a clear answer.

gddGap: The GDD names Overseer Halden Varr, "The Architect of Rust", as the Main Boss (Corporate Tower command chamber, theme: authority, mastery, hybrid combat) with two phases and named moves, but no stats, numbers or timings. The moves and the 30 percent HP phase trigger are canon; every stat and wind-up below is proposed. GDD wording clashes with the tone rules in places (Rust described as executioners, "brutal"); this entry keeps Varr cold and official, and knocks Zed down rather than harming him lethally. Also: the GDD stance name "Antirush" is probably a typo and is recorded here as the anti-rush-down stance. FINAL BALANCE (tuned against the combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms telegraph as the Tier 0 anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms): 320 HP is about 18 finishers and the top of the curve (grunt 30, Breaker 90, Fang 140, Architect 160); 18 damage on the fast Authority Strike keeps Zed alive for at least 5 hits; 400 ms is the shortest boss wind-up, justified by the GDD "fast startup", and stays above the 300 ms floor. Phase 2 (30 percent HP): moveSpeed x1.15, recoverMs x0.8, damage unchanged, so "relentless" comes from tempo and drones, not one-shots. Numbers final.
name: Overseer Halden Varr
description: The founder of Rust and its Main Boss: a former military strategist who believed order could only be achieved through fear, and who replaced the city officials with Rust loyalists. Phase one: a crisp slate command coat over rust-coated plating, an electrified gauntlet on one fist and an emitter for an energy shield on the other arm, a tall cyan visor. Phase two: full oxidized armour, heavier and more boxy, with drones circling. Cold, symmetrical and official. Fought in the Corporate Tower command chamber.
behaviour: Two-phase final boss that fights alongside the units he calls. Phase 1, "Authority": Authority Strike (electrified gauntlet punch, high damage, knockback, fast startup); Command Shield (energy shield that blocks all frontal attacks and must be flanked or broken); Command Override (summons Rust Grunts, Watchers or Copper Fangs, Varr fights alongside them, counted against the attacker cap); Adaptive Counter (changes stance based on Zed's behaviour: anti-air stance if Zed jumps too often, anti-rush-down stance if Zed charges in, anti-combo stance if Zed strings long combos, forcing Zed to vary his play). Phase 2, "Rust Protocol", triggered at 30 percent HP: Hybrid Assault (uses moves from every Rust unit type: Breaker slam, Watcher taser shot, Copper Fang gauntlet combo and Overseer-style control attacks); Drone Command (summons elite drones that fire lasers in bullet-hell patterns); Rust Collapse super move (Varr overloads his armour for a massive area explosion, the arena walls electrify, and the final phase becomes relentless). Zed is knocked down and pushed back by these, never put down for good.
telegraph: Authority Strike: 400 ms wind-up, gauntlet drawn back and crackling. Command Shield: shield emitter glows and hums before it deploys, 500 ms. Command Override: 800 ms, console pulse rings mark where units appear. Adaptive Counter: a visible stance change with a colour cue (the stance is shown, never hidden). Drones: 600 ms lock-on line before each laser. Rust Collapse: a long 1500 ms charge, armour cracks glowing, a huge red ground danger zone, and the walls flash a warning before they electrify. Every attack keeps the red telegraph icon, scaled 1.4 times, with the standard tint and thicker outline.
weakness: Flank or break the Command Shield with heavy attacks; clear summoned units to focus Varr; vary the approach so Adaptive Counter never settles on one stance; in phase two dodge the Collapse zone and the drone lanes, then punish in the recovery. Rewards every pillar: combos, block, dodge, parry and wave-clearing under pressure.

gddGap: The GDD names Overseer Kade Voss, "The Eye of the Market" (theme: surveillance, prediction, drones, holograms; arena: Neon Market control hub with screens, drones and hologram emitters). Phase 1 "Data Acquisition": Predictive Strike, Drone Swarm, Hologram Decoy, Data Spike. Phase 2 "System Override" at 50 percent HP: Predictive Lockdown, Drone Fusion, Hologram Assault, System Crash (super). Combat contract support needed: bullet-hell drone entities with their own HP, hologram decoys that can later attack, a 10 second special-meter lockout on Zed, a safe-zone floor hazard, and moving electric pillars. All Overseers are district bosses, strategic masterminds and Varr's inner circle, with a tactical, oppressive combat style and unique mechanics (GDD role line). Moves, phases, phase trigger and arena are canon; all numbers and timings are proposed. Zed is knocked down and pushed back, never put down for good. FINAL BALANCE (same method as Varr and the other tier 3 items; combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms as the anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms; below Varr at 320 HP): 200 HP (a mobile ranged boss, fragile once reached), 10 damage per shot or pillar, 1000 ms Predictive Strike wind-up (the GDD says the shot fires after 1 s, so the red line is the telegraph). Numbers final.
name: Overseer Kade Voss
description: A Rust Overseer of the Neon Market in a slate command coat with steel shoulder plates and a wide cyan visor that projects a thin red scan line. Cold, symmetrical and boxy, working from a control hub of screens, drones and hologram emitters, with a flicker in the real body that gives the copies away. Official, not armoured.
behaviour: Phase 1, "Data Acquisition": Predictive Strike (the visor scans Zed and draws a red line where it expects him to move; after 1 second a laser shot fires along that line, forcing Zed to break patterns); Drone Swarm (summons 3 to 5 orbiting drones that fire small taser bolts, can be destroyed, and create bullet-hell pressure); Hologram Decoy (creates 2 hologram copies that mimic his movement but do not attack, while the real Voss flickers slightly, so Zed must identify the target); Data Spike (slams a hand into a console and electric pillars erupt from the ground in a pattern that changes each use, punishing a player who stands still). Phase 2, "System Override", at 50 percent HP (arena lights dim, drones turn red): Predictive Lockdown (the visor locks on and Zed's special meter is disabled for 10 seconds, Voss grows more aggressive, forcing reliance on fundamentals); Drone Fusion (remaining drones merge into a slow MegaDrone that fires sweeping laser beams, a second boss-like threat); Hologram Assault (holograms now attack with a weak punch or shot, while the real Voss attacks at the same time, for chaotic multi-angle pressure); System Crash super move (overloads the arena grid, the whole floor electrifies except safe zones that shift every second, forcing constant movement). Pressure is knockdown and pushback only.
telegraph: Predictive Strike: 1000 ms, the red predicted-path line stays visible the whole time. Drone Swarm: 700 ms console flash, drones spawn with a cyan ring. Hologram Decoy: 500 ms shimmer. Data Spike: 600 ms, glowing floor tiles mark every pillar spot. Predictive Lockdown: 600 ms visor lock-on ring. Drone Fusion: 800 ms merge flash. Hologram Assault: 500 ms. System Crash: 1500 ms, the floor flashes and the safe zones glow green before every shift. All keep the red telegraph icon scaled 1.4 times with the standard tint.
weakness: Break the pattern: change direction before the 1 second line fires. Pick off drones, find the real Voss by the flicker, stay moving on the pillars. In phase 2 rely on basics while the special meter is locked, and follow the glowing safe zones during System Crash.

gddGap: The GDD names Overseer Rhea Calder, "The Iron Matron" (theme: industrial power, machinery, brute force; arena: factory floor with conveyors, crushers and steam vents). Phase 1 "Discipline Through Strength": Forge Hammer Smash, Hydraulic Grab, Steam Burst Armor, Conveyor Trap. Phase 2 "Factory Protocol" at 40 percent HP: Overclock Mode, Industrial Barrage, Furnace Slam (super). Combat contract support needed: traveling floor shockwave, guard break, grab/throw with super armour during startup, temporary invulnerability, conveyor and crusher hazards, off-screen arm attacks, and delayed exploding floor cracks. All Overseers are district bosses, strategic masterminds and Varr's inner circle, with a tactical, oppressive combat style and unique mechanics (GDD role line). Moves, phases, phase trigger and arena are canon; all numbers and timings are proposed. Zed is knocked down and pushed back, never put down for good. FINAL BALANCE (same method as Varr and the other tier 3 items; combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms as the anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms; below Varr at 320 HP): 260 HP (the tankiest of the four, slow brute), 20 damage on the Forge Hammer (the highest single hit besides the super, which is about 20 percent of a 100 HP player), 900 ms wind-up and 1300 ms recovery for the "slow but devastating" hammer. Numbers final.
name: Overseer Rhea Calder
description: A Rust Overseer of the factory districts in a heavy slate exosuit with steel plating and hydraulic arms, a massive hammer on one arm and steam vents along the back. Cold, symmetrical and boxy, a cyan visor in a squared helmet. Her suit glows red in the second phase.
behaviour: Phase 1, "Discipline Through Strength": Forge Hammer Smash (massive overhead hammer strike; a shockwave travels across the floor and can break guard; slow but devastating); Hydraulic Grab (exosuit arms extend with long reach to grab Zed, leading into a slam or throw, with super armour during startup); Steam Burst Armor (vents steam for temporary invulnerability and pushes Zed back, used to reset pressure); Conveyor Trap (activates conveyor belts that carry Zed toward crushers or hazards, forcing repositioning). Phase 2, "Factory Protocol", at 40 percent HP (exosuit glows red): Overclock Mode (attack speed up: faster hammer swings, shorter grab startup, more frequent steam bursts); Industrial Barrage (robotic arms from the background punch or grab from off-screen, telegraphed by flashing lights, adding multi-directional threats); Furnace Slam super move (leaps and slams the hammer down, molten cracks spread over the floor and explode after 2 seconds for high damage over a large area). Zed is knocked down, thrown or pushed, never put down for good.
telegraph: Forge Hammer Smash: 900 ms, hammer raised overhead with a red shockwave lane on the floor. Hydraulic Grab: 600 ms, arms visibly extend with a red reach line, super armour shown as a bright outline. Steam Burst Armor: 400 ms hiss and a white puff before it deploys. Conveyor Trap: 700 ms, belt arrows light up. Overclock Mode: the red glow itself, and phase 2 wind-ups run at 80 percent but never below 300 ms. Industrial Barrage: 700 ms flashing lights at each arm position. Furnace Slam: 1500 ms leap and a red crack preview, then the 2 second countdown on every crack. All keep the red telegraph icon scaled 1.4 times.
weakness: Dodge out of the shockwave lane and punish the long hammer recovery. Do not poke during the grab startup (super armour) and do not wait inside a steam burst (invulnerable). Read the conveyors, watch the flashing lights for the arms, and leave the cracks before they blow.

gddGap: The GDD names Overseer Silas Wren, "The Whisper on the Rooftops" (theme: mobility, stealth, vertical control; arena: rooftop platforms, zip lines and breakable ledges). Phase 1 "Silent Hunter": GrappleDash Barrage, Skyline Snare, Silent Step, Rooftop Execution. Phase 2 "Ghost of the Skyline" at 50 percent HP: Grapple Clone, Shadow Pulse, Vanish Storm (super). Combat contract support needed: platform and vertical movement with attacks from above or behind, restraint traps, a semi-invisible state, a guaranteed-critical flag (no critical hit exists in the contract), afterimages that perform fake attacks, and multiple silhouettes. Tone note: the GDD move name "Rooftop Execution" is kept as canon but should be shown as a dive attack that knocks Zed down, never a lethal blow; the owner may prefer to rename it. All Overseers are district bosses, strategic masterminds and Varr's inner circle, with a tactical, oppressive combat style and unique mechanics (GDD role line). Moves, phases, phase trigger and arena are canon; all numbers and timings are proposed. Zed is knocked down and pushed back, never put down for good. FINAL BALANCE (same method as Varr and the other tier 3 items; combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms as the anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms; below Varr at 320 HP): 180 HP (the most fragile, the fastest at 120 move speed), 14 damage, 400 ms wind-up for the "very fast" grapple dash, kept above the 300 ms floor; the dive uses 600 ms so grounded players can read it. Numbers final.
name: Overseer Silas Wren
description: A Rust Overseer of the rooftops, lean in a dark slate suit with a grapple launcher on each forearm and a slim cyan visor, much lighter than the other Overseers. Cold, symmetrical and boxy even when moving fast, with a faint cyan outline that stays visible when he turns semi-invisible.
behaviour: Phase 1, "Silent Hunter": GrappleDash Barrage (zips between platforms, attacking from above or from behind, very fast, hard to punish without prediction); Skyline Snare (throws electrified wire traps that restrict movement and can immobilise Zed briefly, forcing careful navigation); Silent Step (turns semi-invisible with only a faint outline, and his next attack is a guaranteed critical, used unpredictably); Rooftop Execution (a dive attack from above for high damage that creates a shockwave, punishing players who stay on the ground). Phase 2, "Ghost of the Skyline", at 50 percent HP (faster and quieter): Grapple Clone (afterimages left when he grapples perform fake attacks, while the real Silas attacks from an unexpected angle); Shadow Pulse (releases a burst of energy that knocks Zed back and resets spacing, used after combos); Vanish Storm super move (disappears completely, multiple silhouettes attack from all sides, and the real Silas finishes with a heavy strike; requires reading patterns). Zed is knocked down and pushed back, never put down for good.
telegraph: GrappleDash Barrage: 400 ms, the grapple line shows and a red marker lands at the destination platform. Skyline Snare: 600 ms, the wire glints and a red strip marks the trap. Silent Step: 500 ms shimmer, then the faint outline stays. The critical hit after Silent Step has its own 500 ms cyan flash. Rooftop Execution: 600 ms, a red shadow circle grows on the floor under the dive. Grapple Clone: 500 ms. Shadow Pulse: 450 ms ring. Vanish Storm: 1200 ms fade, silhouettes each get a red icon and the real one gets a heavier outline. All keep the red telegraph icon scaled 1.4 times.
weakness: Watch the red shadow under the dive and stay off the ground marker; check the outline during Silent Step and block or dodge the flashed critical. Keep moving through snares, hit the real Silas (the one with the heavier outline) and punish him after Shadow Pulse resets spacing.

gddGap: The GDD names Overseer Dr. Maren Holt, "The Voice of Compliance" (theme: chemicals, toxins, psychological control; arena: undercity lab with gas vents, toxin pools and fog zones). Phase 1 "Chemical Control": Fear Gas, Obedience Mist, Toxin Burst, Sedative Shot. Phase 2 "Doctor's Orders" at 40 percent HP: NeuroFog, Corrosive Wave, Compliance Protocol (super). Combat contract support needed: control distortion and reversal on Zed, screen blur and reduced vision, movement slow and reduced dodge distance, lingering and spreading area damage zones, an attack-speed debuff, stealth attacks, damage over time, and damage that also hits Holt herself. Tone note: these are comic-book gas effects (blur, slow, reversed controls), not graphic harm; keep them clearly non-lethal. All Overseers are district bosses, strategic masterminds and Varr's inner circle, with a tactical, oppressive combat style and unique mechanics (GDD role line). Moves, phases, phase trigger and arena are canon; all numbers and timings are proposed. Zed is knocked down and pushed back, never put down for good. FINAL BALANCE (same method as Varr and the other tier 3 items; combat contract: Zed light 6-7, heavy 12, finisher 18 damage; grunt 30 HP / 8 damage / 450 ms as the anchor; every telegraph at least 300 ms; below Varr at 320 HP): 190 HP, 9 damage (the lowest, since her pressure is debuffs and zones), 600 ms wind-up for the vial throw. Numbers final.
name: Overseer Dr. Maren Holt
description: A Rust Overseer of the undercity lab in a slate lab coat over light plating, a rebreather and a cyan visor, a belt of chemical vials and a dart launcher on one forearm. Cold, symmetrical and official; her suit glows with pressure in the second phase. Purple and green fog marks her gas.
behaviour: Phase 1, "Chemical Control": Fear Gas (releases purple fog that distorts Zed's controls and blurs the screen, forcing careful movement); Obedience Mist (green fog that slows movement, reduces dodge distance and makes combos harder); Toxin Burst (throws chemical vials that create lingering area damage zones, controlling space); Sedative Shot (fires a dart that reduces Zed's attack speed, used to punish aggressive players). Phase 2, "Doctor's Orders", at 40 percent HP (suit glows with chemical pressure): NeuroFog (the whole arena fills with fog, Zed's vision is reduced, Holt becomes harder to track and uses stealth attacks); Corrosive Wave (throws a large vial that explodes into spreading acid that damages both Zed and Holt, forcing repositioning); Compliance Protocol super move (releases a massive chemical cloud, Zed's controls reverse, damage over time, and Holt becomes extremely aggressive). Effects ease off when Zed clears the fog; Zed is knocked down and pushed back, never put down for good.
telegraph: Fear Gas: 700 ms vent hiss and purple puff. Obedience Mist: 700 ms green puff. Toxin Burst: 600 ms, red ground circle where the vial lands. Sedative Shot: 450 ms, a thin line to Zed. NeuroFog: 900 ms, vents glow before the fog rolls in. Corrosive Wave: 700 ms, a red spreading-radius preview. Compliance Protocol: 1500 ms charge, a huge cloud outline and a "controls reversed" icon on the HUD before it reaches Zed. All keep the red telegraph icon scaled 1.4 times.
weakness: Stay out of the lingering zones and clear the fog by moving upwind of the vents. Do not over-commit while slowed or sedated; block or dodge the dart. Use Corrosive Wave against Holt by herding her into the acid, and learn the reversed controls during Compliance Protocol.
